input.question: Helicopter tail rotors? Why are they so important?
input.ground_truth: The torque required for the main rotor has an opposite torque acting on the rest of the frame. That is, if the main rotor is spinning clockwise, the rest of the frame is being torqued counterclockwise. The tail rotor acts to counteract the torque and keep the frame pointing in the right direction.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Helicopter tail rotors? Why are they so important?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Here’s how I’d explain it to a 5-year-old:

A helicopter has a big spinning thing on the back called a "tail rotor." This tail rotor is very important because it helps the helicopter fly straight.

When the big helicopter blades spin around to lift the helicopter up, they also want to make the whole helicopter spin around really fast, like a top! But we don’t want the helicopter to spin around while flying.

The tail rotor is like a little helper. It spins the other way and pushes the air so that the helicopter doesn’t spin. That’s why the tail rotor is super important—it keeps the helicopter flying straight and steady!
